name: Stationarity and ARMA
description: Test whether a series is stable over time and model how it remembers its past.

requires.why: The Dickey-Fuller test is a regression on lagged values, read like a fitted line.
Computes returns and differences with pandas shift, pct_change and rolling means.

lessonNames.l1-returns-not-prices: Why we model returns, not prices
lessonNames.l2-what-stays-the-same: What stays the same over time

lessonObjectives.l1-returns-not-prices: Compare a price series with its returns and see which one is stable.
lessonObjectives.l2-what-stays-the-same: Define weak stationarity and judge it from a chart.
lessonObjectives.l3-unit-root: Run an augmented Dickey-Fuller test and read its result.
lessonObjectives.l4-differencing: Difference a series to make it stationary.
lessonObjectives.l5-own-past: Compute and plot the autocorrelation function.
lessonObjectives.l6-pure-noise: Recognise white noise and test for it with Ljung-Box.
lessonObjectives.l7-today-depends-on-yesterday: Simulate and fit an AR(1) model.
lessonObjectives.l8-partial: Use the partial autocorrelation function to choose an AR order.
lessonObjectives.l9-shocks-that-linger: Simulate and identify an MA(1) model.
lessonObjectives.l10-combining: Fit an ARMA model and choose its orders by AIC.
lessonObjectives.l11-forecast-intervals: Forecast with an ARMA model and see the interval widen with the horizon.
lessonObjectives.l12-half-life: Estimate how fast a series mean-reverts from its AR(1) coefficient.
